blocks.text: Blue Owl Technology Finance Corp. | Coverage: BDCs / technology direct lending    |    Data to 14 Aug 2026

Verdict: OTF stabilised this quarter (NAV flat at $16.48; non-accruals of 0.6% at cost still the lowest of the six peers), but the industry's credit tail is deteriorating and the portfolio is concentrated precisely in the application-software layer where AI pressure is greatest. Holding assessed as “sound overall, continued monitoring required”: hold the position unchanged, track against the Section 4 trigger lines — no action needed until a line is breached.
OTF key metrics at a glance

rows: Spreads stabilised; valuation gains turned positive +$0.03
First quarter inside the 0.90–1.25x target range

blocks.note: Source: OTF Q2'26 and Q1'26 10-Qs, Q2'26 earnings presentation; share price = exchange close via stockanalysis.com.

Left: NAV bridge — the $0.10 dividend gap largely refilled by $0.05 repurchase accretion, with valuation gains turning positive. Right: NII dividend-coverage trend — cash coverage of the base dividend at 86%.

items: Section 36(b) excessive-fee lawsuit filed 6/18 (S.D.N.Y.): alleges advisory fees +191% over 2021–25 vs assets +134%, with fees charged on ~$43mm of PIK accruals (~25% of NII). No 36(b) plaintiff has ever prevailed — near-term economics limited, but it introduces Level-3 valuation discovery risk.

Q2 results (8/5): NAV flat at $16.48; NII $0.30; $55mm repurchased in the quarter, ~$170mm over three quarters; shares +7.4% to $11.20 on the day. Management noted the 0.7x discount implies a ~40% portfolio default rate (at 50c recovery).
Funding-side validation: $500mm of 6.50% Oct-2029 unsecured notes issued in June (KBRA BBB) — IG market access at mid-6% coupons despite sector-wide redemption pressure.

Sister-fund redemption pressure stabilising but unresolved: OCIC requests 21.9%→18.8%, OTIC 40.7%→38.1%, $4.7bn combined (1Q: $5.4bn); the 5% cap was hit for a second straight quarter; Moody's cut OCIC's outlook to negative (Baa2 affirmed).

Industry losses crystallising: Medallia handed to lenders ($5.1bn equity wiped out; prior BDC marks 74–79c); Affordable Care's $1.4bn default; KKR's $300mm injection into FS KKR sets a sponsor-backstop template.

rows: Deterioration concentrates in the tail: BDCs >8% rose from 8% to 11%
Back to the 2025 average +8bp; JPM credit desk overweight while its equity desk stays cautious — the debt-vs-equity split is the key live debate
Industry PIK (% total income / % net income)
Flat on gross, rising on net — dividend quality is being quietly eroded
Median software borrower leverage (vs all sectors)
Industry stress sits exactly in OTF's core lane
50% rated ≤B−; the four houses' common catalyst is the maturity wall, not current defaults
Rate-cut-driven and reversible — the rate path repairing borrower coverage also erodes OTF asset yields
blocks.note: Source: JPM / Morgan Stanley / Goldman Sachs / BofA research, Apr–Jul 2026 (11 reports on file); Fitch, Lincoln and S&P credit-estimate samples.

Left: BDC industry non-accruals at a five-year high, with the tail (>8% share) jumping faster than the mean. Right: share price since IPO — OTF −30.8%, worst of the BDC set and the visual source of the 0.70x discount.

items: The transmission channel is valuation, not default: ~48% of OTF's fair value sits in the two end-markets with the heaviest credit migration (software 32.8% + healthcare tech 12.4% + healthcare services 2.9%). Industry software spread widening reprices OTF's Level-3 marks and the equity discount first — last quarter's $0.84 NAV write-down was spread-driven, and partially recovered this quarter (+$0.03).

OTF's own data remains the counter-evidence: weighted borrower EBITDA of $291mm (+2.1% QoQ, +15.9% YoY) is still growing; PIK is down two straight quarters; non-accruals at fair value are 0.1%, an order of magnitude below the 2.8% industry average. But $38.7mm of the EBITDA gain came from pre-4Q25 consolidation effects — only +$1.2mm over the last two quarters: growth is slowing, not yet falling.

Three changes worth noting: net leverage entered the target range for the first time (0.93x; incremental leverage now billed at the lower 1.00% management-fee tier); base-dividend cash coverage is only 86%, so the payout rests on rising leverage; specials end from Q4'26, resetting the yield from 14.0% to 12.2% (9.7% → 8.5% on NAV), which may trigger rotation by income holders.

blocks.note: Each company's Q2'26 10-Q; BXSL / OBDC / TSLX / GBDC disclose semi-annual or FYTD NAV comparisons. OTF software exposure of 32.8% (GICS) is the highest of the six, vs ARCC 22.0%, BXSL 18.9%, OBDC ~18%; TSLX does not break out software. OBDC dividend $0.37→$0.31 (plus $0.02 supplemental), TSLX $0.46→$0.42, GBDC $0.39→$0.33.

blocks.html: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action
blocks.text: 4. Our Position: Assessment, Watch List & Action

items: Overall assessment: sound, monitoring required. Credit (non-accruals, PIK direction, borrower earnings) is the best of the six; valuation shows the deepest discount at 0.70x, with sell-side targets of $11.50–17.00 (consensus ~$13.6, flat to +47% vs spot); the risks are application-software concentration (the application layer is roughly half of portfolio fair value) and the 36(b) lawsuit — both “watch items”, not “action items”.

blocks.text: Watch list (next-quarter checks and trigger lines)

rows: If discovery begins, assess Level-3 disclosure risk
Either way a management signal; fold into next summary

blocks.text: Action: hold, no change. The 0.70x discount is the market pre-pricing application-software concentration, not a signal of OTF-specific credit deterioration — its non-accruals, PIK direction and borrower earnings all beat peers. If the discount widens below 0.60x or non-accruals breach 2%, take the position back to IC.
